role: SS38 replacement for the Fed subset of the BIS speech corpus, which is licensed NONCOMMERCIAL-ONLY
licence_note: NO copyright notice found on the speech pages, the About page, or any /publications/copyright.htm (404); federalreserve.gov serves NO robots.txt (404 HTML). This is an ABSENCE of restriction plus the 17 USC 105 US-Government posture -- it is NOT an explicit reuse grant, and is recorded as measured rather than as a licence certificate. It is materially freer than BIS's verbatim noncommercial-only clause, which is the point of this replacement hunt.

scope_verified.board_only_evidence: all 42 speaker strings carry a Board title (Chairman/Chair/Vice Chair/Governor); ZERO regional Reserve Bank presidents appear (no Bullard, Kashkari, Williams, Bostic, Daly)

coverage_vs_bis.residual_interpretation: the ~646 post-2006 rows BIS holds and the Board index does not are regional Reserve Bank speeches (12 banks, each with its own public site) plus BIS's own non-Board US material; the 591 pre-2006 rows predate this JSON index. The replacement is PARTIAL and the residual is ENUMERABLE -- 12 named successor sources, not a dead end (SS38).

known_failure_modes: the JSON array's LAST element is a metadata row {'updateDate': ...} with no 'd' key -- a naive comprehension over the array raises KeyError (it did here); filter on key presence, never on index

SPEAKER STRINGS ARE NOT NORMALISED and fragment one person across title changes: Jerome H. Powell appears under 4 distinct strings (Governor/Chair/Chairman/Chair Pro Tempore), Quarles under 4, Bowman/Barr/Yellen/Brainard/Kohn/Clarida/Jefferson under 2 each. A speaker-fixed-effects or per-speaker tone panel that groups on the raw string SILENTLY SPLITS one speaker into several entities
'Chairman  Ben S. Bernanke' carries a DOUBLE SPACE and is a 2nd distinct string for Bernanke -- whitespace-normalise before any grouping
index is Board-only: treating it as 'the Fed' understates FOMC-relevant commentary, because regional presidents are voting members
dates are US M/D/YYYY with a time component; the file is served with a UTF-8 BOM (encoding='utf-8-sig' required)
